The PR description states "the ask now applies only when an `env` wrapper or per-command Git configuration selected the unresolved directory" and "shell-control or redirect-uncertain commits only warn" (citing `test_shell_control_commit_on_open_checkout_only_warns`), so the implementation contradicts the documented contract for the `env + shell-control` combination.
  Why it fails at runtime: A user running `if true; then env FOO=bar git commit -m x; fi` will receive an unexpected `permissionDecision: ask` even though `FOO=bar` does not change the working directory. The existing `test_shell_control_commit_on_open_checkout_only_warns` does not exercise this combination, so the test still passes — but the documented behavior diverges from the implementation for this edge case. The cost is one extra permission prompt; the user can still approve, so this is not a security regression.
